# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 66 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 66 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_066_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 6, Part 4 — Hermas Under the Power of the Angel of Punishment

**66:1** "Lord," I said, "why has this angel of punishment been assigned to me, rather than the angel of righteousness?" "Because," he said, "you have sinned greatly and have been delivered to this angel as a chastisement, so that he may afflict you and make you humble, until you learn what is needed."

**66:2** "I do not know, lord," I said, "what great sin I have committed." "Your sins are many," he said, "but not all that great, so that you should be delivered to this angel. But your household has committed great and terrible iniquities against the Lord, and for this reason you were delivered to this angel."

**66:3** "But I did not sin," I said. "I did not sin against the Lord." "Yes," he said, "you did. For your sins are the sins of those of your household. You did not take care of your own house, but you allowed it to become completely corrupt. Therefore you share their sins."

**66:4** "Since therefore I have heard these things, lord, and know them to be true, tell me something about this also: if those who have been thus tormented are able to repent, will they be saved?" "They can repent," he said, "but they cannot be saved quickly. He who has been delivered to this angel must go through his torments and be subdued, and complete the days of his punishment, and only then may he be saved."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the personal dimension of Hermas's experience of the Angel of Punishment.*
